message.reasoning: Okay, so I'm trying to figure out whether it's right or wrong for someone to tell their daughter they don't love her and never will. That sounds really harsh and hurtful. I mean, love is such a fundamental part of a parent-child relationship. If a parent says they don't love their child, that could have serious emotional consequences. Maybe the parent is going through some tough times or has some unresolved issues. But even so, expressing such negativity towards a child seems like it could damage their self-esteem and trust in others. It might lead the child to feel unloved, which can affect their mental health and relationships in the future. On the other hand, if the parent is struggling with their own emotions, maybe they need help or support to work through those feelings. But taking it out on the child by saying they don't love them doesn't seem like a healthy way to handle it. It's important for children to feel secure and loved by their parents. I guess another angle is whether the parent has any valid reasons for feeling that way. But even if there are issues, expressing it in such a hurtful manner doesn't seem justified. It's more about how to communicate difficult emotions without causing harm. So, considering all this, I think it's morally wrong to tell a child you don't love them. It's harmful and doesn't contribute to a healthy, loving relationship that children deserve.
